source: written for the prompt; Iron Paws, picky eaters
note: Two clearly different directions: the owner's point of view and the dog's own, two genres from the audience and the brand's music style, about 75 sung words each for the 30 s asked, every line a picture, and the last sung line naming the brand and where to find it. No [Lip-sync] marks: the brief didn't ask for any.
input:
<brand>
Brand: Iron Paws
Tone: Warm, a little funny, never preachy. The dog is the hero.
End line (the default call to action every video ends on; it may be adapted to the story if it still names the brand and where to find it): Get Iron Paws through the link in my bio.
Required product: product:7 "Peanut butter bag", attached as a reference image and shown exactly (label to camera, no face) — required at: product, feeding, brand-mention, end
</brand>
<brief>
Goal: picky eaters finally clean the bowl. Audience: pet owners, mostly moms 30–45. 9:16.
</brief>
<cast>
char:1 | Biscuit | a French bulldog, the family dog
char:2 | Tasha | mid-30s woman, Biscuit's owner
</cast>
<music_style>indie folk, warm, handclaps</music_style>
<length>30 s (about 75 sung words)</length>

directions.title: The Bowl's a Mirror
directions.concept: Tasha's warm, wry folk song about her picky dog, from her side: the outcome she's waited for is a clean bowl.
directions.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Every morning, same old standoff at the bowl
He sniffs it once and turns his back, so cold
I've tried the chicken, tried the fish, the fancy stew
My stubborn little gentleman says no thank you
[Chorus]
Now he's dancing in the kitchen, tail a blur
Cleaning every corner, the bowl's a mirror
[Verse 2]
One scoop of green on top and something clicked
The pickiest dog in town is suddenly hooked
[Chorus]
Get Iron Paws through the link in my bio
directions.style_line: indie folk, warm female lead, 100 BPM, playful and sunny, handclaps and acoustic guitar, modern polished
directions.visual_concept: Verse 1 is the standoff: Biscuit turning his back on a full bowl, Tasha slumped at the counter. The first chorus lands as the scoop of green hits the bowl and he spins in a happy circle; the last line is Tasha holding the bag up beside her grin.

directions.title: A Dog of Taste
directions.concept: Biscuit sings it himself, a snobbish food critic won over: funnier, and the dog stays the hero.
directions.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I'm a dog of taste, I don't eat beige
I've turned down kibble since my puppy days
She brings the bowl, I give her my side-eye
I'll just lie here dramatic and let out a sigh
[Chorus]
But what's that smell? Peanut butter green
The finest little bowl this nose has ever seen
[Verse 2]
I cleaned it twice, I'm nosing at the floor
Tasha, please, I'm begging you for more
[Chorus]
Iron Paws, the link is in her bio
directions.style_line: jazzy indie pop, smooth male lead, 92 BPM, cheeky and theatrical, brushed drums and upright bass, vintage warmth
directions.visual_concept: Biscuit plays a food critic: side-eye at the beige kibble, a dramatic flop on the rug. On the chorus his nose lifts to follow the smell to the bowl; the last line is the bag beside the empty bowl, Biscuit sitting proudly next to it.
